The '''Trenkwalder Group AG''' is a full-service outsourcing [[human resources]] and personnel employment provider in CEE in 15 [[Europe|European]] countries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fact and Figures {{!}} Trenkwalder |url=https://de.trenkwalder.com/en-DE/about-us/fact-and-figures |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=Trenkwalder Germany |language=en-DE}}</ref> Trenkwalder expanded through numerous acquisitions in Austria and abroad and has more than 200 locations. The company is a market leader in [[Austria]] and [[Hungary]]. Since 2011, it has been part of the Droege Group.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Salzburger Nachrichten |date=2023-09-21 |title=Professionals Sought Worldwide |url=https://www.sn.at/leben/karriere/oesterreich-fachkraefte-ausland-145664086 |access-date=2024-07-23 |language=de}}</ref>

== Company history ==

=== 1985 to 2002 ===
The [[Engineer]] Richard Trenkwalder founded the company in 1985 in [[Schwadorf]]. Through professional activities abroad, he was familiar with the leasing of specialists. He initially operated his company with around 30 employees.<ref name="WiBla-2000-08-26">''Trenkwalder aims to achieve 2.4 billion ATS in sales. Personnel leasing company expects further growth this year.'' In: ''[[Wirtschaftsblatt]].'' 26 August 2000.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mark Pollok Appointed CEO of Trenkwalder Group AG |url=https://www.leadersnet.at/news/65427,mark-pollok-zum-ceo-der-trenkwalder-group-ag-ernannt.html |access-date=2024-07-23 |language=de}}</ref> Trenkwalder is one of the companies that have held a [[license]] for personnel leasing since 1988, when these were first granted in Austria.<ref name="Passauer">''Temporary work Trenkwalder: Growing with the trend of the times.'' In: ''[[Passauer Neue Presse]].'' 24 July 2004.</ref>

By establishing [[Branch office|branches]] and through [[Merger and acquisition|acquisitions]] and partial acquisitions of competitors in Austria, the company expanded in its home country. In 1998, Trenkwalder ranked behind Austria's ''Manpower'' (now: ''Powerserv'')<ref>Two companies fought for years in Austria over the [[Trademark|rights to the brand]] ''Manpower''. This legal dispute was only resolved in 2006. See {{cite web|access-date=2016-08-18 |date=2006-02-16 |title=Manpower Austria is now called Powerserv |url=https://derstandard.at/2328704/Manpower-Austria-heisst-nun-Powerserv |website=[[derStandard.at]]}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> and [[Adecco]] in third place; in 2000, it became the market leader in Austria.<ref>''I am a Trenkwalder! The Werther campaign for the personnel agency.'' In: ''[[Horizont (Zeitschrift)|Horizont]].'' 24 March 2000.</ref>

In 1992, Trenkwalder opened its first foreign branch in the [[Slovakia|Slovak]] capital [[Bratislava]].<ref name="WiBla-2000-08-26" /> Since 1999, the company has been active in [[Germany]] and Hungary.<ref name="ORF">{{cite web|access-date=2016-08-18 |date=2013-02-20 |title=Around 70,000 employees |url=https://orf.at/stories/2167656/2167708/ |website=[[Austrian Broadcasting Corporation#Internet|orf.at]]}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> The following year, it entered the market in [[Czech Republic|Czechia]]<ref name="Staatswappen">{{Webarchive |url=http://www.staatswappen.at/index.asp?p=staatswappen&m=79542 |text=Information about Trenkwalder |wayback=20161019152240 |archiv-bot=2018-12-02 08:29:46 InternetArchiveBot}} on the website about Austrian State Coat of Arms bearers (retrieved on 18 August 2016).</ref> and in [[Italy]],<ref>''Personnel service provider Trenkwalder. Boom in Italy. 45 percent sales growth planned for the current year'', ''Wirtschaftsblatt'' of 23 February 2001.</ref> and in 2001, it began market entry in [[Slovenia]].<ref name="Staatswappen" />

From 1998 to 2000, Trenkwalder was among the fastest-growing companies in Europe each year.<ref name="WiBla-1998-12-12">Alexander Foggensteiner: ''Trenkwalder plans growth from 800 million to 6.4 billion. Europe's 500: Personnel provider Trenkwalder ranks seventh'', ''Wirtschaftsblatt'' of 12 December 1998.</ref><ref>''Trenkwalder grows fastest'', [[Der Standard]] of 31 March 2000. ''Trenkwalder aims to be the industry leader in Central Eastern Europe by 2003. Lower Austrian personnel leasing company among Europe's growth champions'', [[Wiener Zeitung]] of 8 June 2001. {{cite web|access-date=2016-08-18 |date=2002-09-13 |title=Trenkwalder remained growth champion in 2001 |url=https://www.tagblatt-wienerzeitung.at/nachrichten/wirtschaft/international/178715_Trenkwalder-blieb-2001-Wachstumschampion.html |website=Wiener Zeitung (online)}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --> {{cite web|access-date=2016-08-18 |title=Business of the week from 10.09. to 16.09.2002 |url=http://www.oe-journal.at/Aktuelles/0902/W2/04_bwirt10091609.htm |website=Österreich Journal}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> However, the company's growth stalled in 2001 and 2002. In 1993, the company employed 80 people and had sales of 80 million [[Austrian schilling|ATS]];<ref name="WiBla-1998-12-12" /> by 2002, Trenkwalder had 7,000 employees and generated sales of 192 million euros.<ref name="WiBla-2002-12-31">Verena Kainrath: ''Two deals at the turn of the year. Trenkwalder gets new capital. Entries just before the deadline: CLC and Trenkwalder enter 2003 with new partners'', ''Wirtschaftsblatt'' of 31 December 2002.</ref> The previous rapid growth led to turbulence. Additionally, a large part of the management in Italy temporarily left for a competitor.<ref name="Gewinn-2008-6">Erich Brenner: ''The gazelle that leases 15,000 employees''. In: [[Gewinn (Zeitschrift)|Gewinn]] No. 3/2004 of 1 March 2004; Erich Brenner: ''With inner peace and 91,000 employees''. In: ''Gewinn'' No. 6/2008 of 1 June 2008.</ref>

=== 2003 to 2011 ===
At the beginning of 2003, German Capiton AG<ref>[https://www.capiton.de/<nowiki> Company website].</nowiki></ref> acquired 25.4 percent of the company's shares for 10 million euros. This investment strengthened Trenkwalder's [[Equity (finance)|equity]] and enabled further expansion.<ref name="trend-2-07">''The Resistant''. In: [[Trend (magazine)|trend]] No. 2/2007 of 11 June 2007.</ref> In 2003, the company began operations in [[Croatia]].<ref>''Strong growth in Tyrolean temporary workers'', [[Tiroler Tageszeitung]] of 5 April 2003.</ref> In October 2003, Trenkwalder acquired a majority stake in the Multi-Man Group, becoming the market leader in Hungary.<ref>''Trenkwalder buys up and plans IPO'', [[Kronen Zeitung]] of 11 October 2011; ''Trenkwalder lends'', [[Kurier (newspaper)|Kurier]] of 11 October 2011; ''More temporary workers for shorter production times. Personnel service provider Trenkwalder becomes market leader in Hungary and sees a rosy future for the industry'', [[Die Presse]] of 11 October 2011; ''Trenkwalder on a big shopping spree. Personnel provider grows domestically and abroad'', ''Wirtschaftsblatt'' of 11 October 2011.</ref> In 2004, the company also achieved market leadership in Slovakia. The following year, Trenkwalder became the largest provider in Czechia through the partial acquisition of Kappa People.<ref>''Trenkwalder aims to be the largest. Personnel service provider takes over Czech market leader''. In: ''Kronen Zeitung'' of 20 September 2005; ''Trenkwalder becomes No. 1 in Czechia'', ''Wirtschaftsblatt'' of 20 September 2005; ''Trenkwalder expands'', [[Salzburger Nachrichten]] of 24 September 2005.</ref> In November 2005, Trenkwalder entered the Polish market by purchasing a majority stake in a Polish provider (Partner Sp. z o.o.).<ref>''Trenkwalder aims to conquer the Polish market. Acquisition: Austria's largest personnel provider grows mainly through acquisitions'', Wirtschaftsblatt of 4 November 2005.</ref> Trenkwalder also started operations in [[Romania]]<ref>''Expansion in Romania'', ''Die Presse'' of 29 April 2006.</ref> and [[Serbia]] in 2005. The partial acquisition (80 percent) of MSE Personal Services AG marked the company's entry into the [[Liechtenstein]] market in early 2006.<ref>''Trenkwalder buys into Liechtenstein'', ''Wirtschaftsblatt'' of 17 January 2006.</ref> Activities also began in [[Switzerland]] in 2006, followed by the acquisition of City Job AG<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2016-08-18 |title=Company Overview of City Job AG |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=32678278 |website=[[Bloomberg L.P.|bloomberg.com]]}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> and the PL Group the following year.<ref>''Trenkwalder buys in Switzerland'', ''Wirtschaftsblatt'' of 15 February 2007; [[M&A Review]], 4/2007, p. 205.</ref> In 2007, Trenkwalder expanded into the markets of [[Bulgaria]],<ref>''Trenkwalder starts in Bulgaria. Acquisition of Correct-Consult Bulgaria EOOD in Sofia'', ''Salzburger Nachrichten'' of 12 May 2007.</ref> [[Montenegro]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[North Macedonia|Macedonia]], and [[Turkey]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2016-08-18 |date=2007-05-21 |title="It was all clear to me" |url=https://derstandard.at/2887875/Fuer-mich-war-das-alles-ganz-klar |website=derStandard.at}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{Webarchive |url=https://group.trenkwalder.com/de/wer-wir-sind/trenkwalder-geschichte |wayback=20161019072311 |text=Information about Trenkwalder's history |archiv-bot=2024-06-01 00:49:09 InternetArchiveBot}} on the company website (retrieved on 18 August 2016).</ref>

In 2007, Trenkwalder also repurchased the shares of Capiton AG for 50 million euros.<ref name="trend-2-07" /> That same year, the corporate structure changed: Trenkwalder International AG became the [[holding company]] for international business, while the business in Austria was spun off into a separate entity, Trenkwalder Personaldienste GmbH.<ref>''Trenkwalder aims for a billion'', ''Salzburger Nachrichten'' of 7 August 2007; ''Trenkwalder restructures'', ''Die Presse'' of 11 August 2007.</ref> The company entered the markets in [[Greece]] and [[Albania]] in 2008, the year in which Trenkwalder, with around 70,000 employees in 450 branches, generated more than 1 billion euros in sales.<ref>Ursula Rischanek: ''Trenkwalder sees opportunities this year as well. Lower Austria: Personnel service provider cracked the billion-euro mark in 2008'', ''Wirtschaftsblatt'' of 14 January 2009; ''Trenkwalder surpasses 1 billion euro mark'', ''Salzburger Nachrichten'' of 14 January 2009.</ref>

The [[2008 financial crisis]] led to 30,000 layoffs at the firm.<ref>Andrea Möchel: ''Personnel service provider: Austria's market leader is optimistic about the future. Trenkwalder sees the crisis as an opportunity'', ''Wirtschaftsblatt'' of 29 September 2009.</ref> Business picked up again from the second quarter of 2009, with the number of employees reaching 53,000 by the end of 2009.<ref name="OÖN-2010-01-30">Sigrid Brandstätter: ''Trenkwalder urgently needs investors'', [[Oberösterreichische Nachrichten]] of 30 January 2010.</ref> Revenue for the 2009 financial year amounted to 790 million euros.<ref name="WiBla-2010-02-02">Bernhard Fischer: ''Trenkwalder seeks financial investor'', ''Wirtschaftsblatt'' of 2 February 2010.</ref> The company sought a financial investor in the following year<ref name="OÖN-2010-01-30" /><ref name="WiBla-2010-02-02" /><ref>''Trenkwalder with investors'', [[Vorarlberger Nachrichten]] of 5 March 2010; Sigrid Brandstätter: ''Personnel provider Trenkwalder wants more time to search for investors'', ''Oberösterreichische Nachrichten'' of 27 November 2010.</ref> and agreed on a comprehensive financing package with banks at the end of the year.<ref>Thorsten Breitkopf: ''Düsseldorf's Droege takes over Trenkwalder'', [[Rheinische Post]] of 18 August 2011.</ref>

=== Since 2011 ===
The sought-after investor was found in 2011: Düsseldorf's Droege Group and Trenkwalder agreed just before Easter 2011 on the sale of more than 75 percent of the company's shares. At the end of 2010, Trenkwalder reported a workforce of 70,000 and sales of around 1 billion euros.<ref>{{cite news |access-date=2016-08-18 |first=Peter |last=Muzik |date=2011-04-25 |title= Frisches Kapital für Trenkwalder |trans-title=Fresh capital for Trenkwalder |url=https://www.tagblatt-wienerzeitung.at/nachrichten/wirtschaft/international/46792_Frisches-Kapital-fuer-Trenkwalder.html |website=[[Wiener Zeitung]] |lang=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=2016-08-18 |first=Stefan |last=Menzel |date=2011-08-17 |trans-title=Handelsblatt: Trenkwalder gets German owner |url=https://www.droege-group.com/de/news-views/aus-der-gruppe/nachricht/article/handelsblatt-trenkwalder-bekommt-deutschen-eigner-1/ |website=Droege Group |lang=de |title=Handelsblatt: Trenkwalder bekommt deutschen Eigner |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204174504/https://www.droege-group.com/de/news-views/aus-der-gruppe/nachricht/article/handelsblatt-trenkwalder-bekommt-deutschen-eigner-1/ |archive-date=2019-02-04}}</ref> The sale was completed in August 2011, following the [[due diligence]] process and approval by the [[Competition law|competition authorities]] and supervisory boards.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2016-08-18 |date=2011-08-17 |title= Neuer Eigner will Personalüberlasser Trenkwalder an die Börse bringen |trans-title=New owner plans to take personnel provider Trenkwalder public |url=https://www.tagblatt-wienerzeitung.at/nachrichten/wirtschaft/oesterreich/390049_Neuer-Eigner-will-Personalueberlasser-Trenkwalder-an-die-Boerse-bringen.html |website=[[Wiener Zeitung]]|lang=de}}</ref>

Since 2012, the company has been transforming from a personnel leasing provider to a universal provider of all human resources (HR) services. This includes [[Human resource management|personnel planning]], recruitment, consulting, and the takeover of HR tasks and processes.

In 2017, the company was renamed: Trenkwalder International AG became Trenkwalder Group AG.<ref>Registered on 9 May 2017 in the [[Company register|commercial register]] (Vienna) for FN 297412 x.{{full citation needed|date=August 2024}}</ref>

== Business activities ==
The ''Staffing'' division<ref>For the range of services offered, see [https://group.trenkwalder.com/de/was-wir-tun the relevant information] on the company's website (retrieved 19 August 2016).</ref> primarily involves the temporary leasing and placement of employees. The ''HR Services'' division offers personnel-related services such as payroll processing or applicant management. As part of ''Personnel Consulting'', Trenkwalder supports strategic [[Human resource management|personnel planning]] and labor market analyses for location selection, including regional labor market characteristics, labor availability, salary assessments, and total labor costs. Trenkwalder Learning offers a wide range of mobile training in self-study and [[Blended learning]] formats in more than 23 languages.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2016-08-18 |date=2010-12-06 |title=Company Profile Trenkwalder |url=https://www.hrweb.at/2010/12/unternehmens-profil-trenkwalder/ |website=hrweb.at}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --> {{cite web|access-date=2016-08-18 |date=2016-06-29 |title=Trenkwalder honored as "Investor in People" for the fourth time |url=https://www.droege-group.com/de/news-views/aus-der-gruppe/nachricht/article/trenkwalder-zum-vierten-mal-als-investor-in-people-ausgezeichnet/ |website=Website of the Droege Group}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>For the Trenkwalder Academy see also ''Special training for big leaps'', [[VDI nachrichten]] No. 27 of 3 July 2009.</ref>

=== Partnerships ===
Wherever joint tasks are to be solved in the labor market, Trenkwalder cooperates with national labor market administrations. An example of this is the collaboration of the Austrian subsidiary with the Employment Service (AMS).

For years, Trenkwalder has cooperated with the [[University for Continuing Education Krems|Danube University Krems]] through its Austrian subsidiary: in 2008, the university course "Personnel Services Management" was established there. It was initially developed specifically for Trenkwalder employees. The program was an [[Master of Business Administration|MBA]] course.<ref>''Continuing education for HR professionals''. In: [[Personalmagazin]] Issue 5/2008, p. 84; ''Golf course or lecture hall''. In: [[Das Österreichische Industriemagazin|Industriemagazin]], Issue 5/2008 p. 84.</ref> A year later, the course was also offered to individuals who were not part of the Trenkwalder staff.<ref>''University course in Krems''. In: ''a3 ECO'', No. 6/2009 of 28 May 2009.</ref> The program continues to be offered in an updated form to this day (as of October 2019).<ref>See the information on education [https://www.donau-uni.ac.at/en/study/personnel-services-management/index.php ''Personnel Services, Personnel Services Management, Professional Workforce Management''] on the Danube University Krems website (retrieved 21 August 2016).</ref>

== Facts and figures ==

=== Customers ===
According to its own information, Trenkwalder works with more than 7,000 customers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fact and Figures {{!}} Trenkwalder |url=https://de.trenkwalder.com/en-DE/about-us/fact-and-figures |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=Trenkwalder Germany |language=en-DE}}</ref>

=== Locations, group, and partners ===
The Trenkwalder Group operates in 16 European countries: Austria, Germany, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Bulgaria, Greece, Croatia, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia, Romania, Czechia, Turkey, Hungary, Kosovo and Netherlands.<ref>{{Cite web |last=anita.staudacher |date=2022-10-19 |title=Trenkwalder-Chef Pollok: Kundenservice aus dem Kosovo |url=https://kurier.at/wirtschaft/trenkwalder-chef-kundenservice-aus-dem-kosovo/402188340 |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=kurier.at |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=2016-08-18 |title=Trenkwalder Group, Countries |url=https://group.trenkwalder.com/de/laender |website=group.trenkwalder.com/de}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> Most of these are in the German-speaking region and [[Central and Eastern European Countries|CEE]] countries. The number of locations exceeds 200.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-10 |title=Arbeitswelt im Umbruch: "Wertschätzung ist in der Wirtschaft die Währung der Zukunft" |url=https://www.kleinezeitung.at/steiermark/graz/17975454/wertschaetzung-ist-in-der-wirtschaft-die-waehrung-der-zukunft |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=www.kleinezeitung.at |language=de}}</ref>

=== Ownership, management, and employees ===
According to the [[Austrian Broadcasting Corporation]], 87.5 percent of the company is owned by the Droege Group, with 12.5 percent held by the Trenkwalder Private Foundation.

Since July 2020, Björn Schlosser has been the sole CEO. Ernest-W. Droege chairs the supervisory board.<ref>[https://group.trenkwalder.com/de/impressum Impressum] of the company website, retrieved on 20 September 2017.</ref>

In 2022, [[Mark Pollok]] was appointed as CEO of Trenkwalder Group AG.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-12-28 |title=Mark Pollok zum CEO der Trenkwalder Group AG ernannt |url=https://www.pressebox.de/pressemitteilung/trenkwalder-personaldienste-gmbh/Mark-Pollok-zum-CEO-der-Trenkwalder-Group-AG-ernannt/boxid/1140726 |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=www.pressebox.de der Trenkwalder Group AG ernannt |url=https://www.leadersnet.at/news/65427,mark-pollok-zum-ceo-der-trenkwalder-group-ag-ernannt.html |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=www.leadersnet.at == Perception ==

=== Sponsorship ===
Trenkwalder was a [[Sponsor (commercial)|sponsor]] of [[TSV 1860 Munich]], a member of the 2nd Bundesliga in Germany. In July 2006, the company initially joined as a presenter.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=2016-08-22 |archive-date=2016-10-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161019072401/http://www.presseportal.de/pm/52307/849331 |author=1860-Presseservice |date=2006-07-17 |title=Trenkwalder Personaldienste is the new presenter of TSV 1860 Munich |url=http://www.presseportal.de/pm/52307/849331 |website=presseportal.de}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> The following year, Trenkwalder became the main sponsor.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=2022-05-25 |archive-date=2016-10-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161019072403/http://www.presseportal.de/pm/52307/1009216 |author=1860-Presseservice |date=2007-06-29 |title=Trenkwalder is the new main sponsor of the Lions |url=https://www.presseportal.de/pm/52307/1009216 |website=presseportal.de}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> Due to the economic crisis, Trenkwalder did not renew the two-year contract.<ref>''Trenkwalder says "goodbye" to 1860 ...'', [[Kärntner Tageszeitung|Neue Kärntner Tageszeitung]] of 7 February 2009; {{cite web |date=2009-03-08 |title=Recession! Shirt sponsor Trenkwalder drops out |url=http://www.tz.de/sport/1860-muenchen/rezession-trikotsponsor-trenkwalder-steigt-aus-98375.html |access-date=2016-08-22 |website=[[Tz (newspaper)|tz]]}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

In Austria, Richard Trenkwalder was involved as president of the club [[ASK Schwadorf]] since 2001. In mid-2008, after promotion to the [[2. Liga (Austria)|First League]] of Austria, the club was named [[FC Admira Wacker Mödling#2008–2014: Ära Trenkwalder und Rückkehr nach Europa|FC Trenkwalder Admira]]. From the 2011/2012 season, it played in the [[Austrian Football Bundesliga]] and in the [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League|2012/2013 UEFA Europa League]] until the third qualifying round.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=2016-08-22 |archive-date=2016-10-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161019072408/http://www.admirawacker.at/verein/geschichte |title=Information about the history of the Admira Wacker club |url=http://www.admirawacker.at/verein/geschichte |website=admirawacker.at}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> The club's [[stadium]] was called the [[BSFZ-Arena|Trenkwalder-Arena]] from 2008 to 2013.

=== Awards ===
Trenkwalder has been honored multiple times as a company:

* Trenkwalder received the State Prize for Employment in 1996.<ref>The company has been a bearer of the [[State Coat of Arms of Austria]] since 22 July 1996, according to {{Webarchive|url=http://www.staatswappen.at/staatswappen.asp?p=&directory=&src_fa=trenkwalder&submit=suchen+...|text=a corresponding database entry|wayback=20161019072413|archiv-bot=2018-12-02 08:29:47 InternetArchiveBot}}.</ref>

* Since 2007<ref>''Seal of approval for Trenkwalder'', ''Salzburger Nachrichten'' of 14 April 2007; ''Trenkwalder certified with IIP. Temporary work company with seal of approval in the Human Resources sector'', ''Der Standard'' of 14 April 2007.</ref> the Austrian subsidiary has been a holder of the [[Seal of approval|seal]] [[Investors in People]]. This quality seal has been confirmed in several recertifications since then. In 2016, Trenkwalder was the first company in Austria to receive the silver award.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2016-08-22 |date=2016-06-29 |title=Trenkwalder honored as "Investor in People" for the fourth time |url=https://www.droege-group.com/de/news-views/aus-der-gruppe/nachricht/article/trenkwalder-zum-vierten-mal-als-investor-in-people-ausgezeichnet/ |website=Website of the Droege Group}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

* The “Entrepreneur of the Year Award”, an award for Austrian companies by [[Ernst & Young]], went to Trenkwalder in 2007 in the Services and Commerce category.<ref>''Best entrepreneurs: Nanoident, Trenkwalder and Polytech'', ''Kurier'' of 13 October 2007; ''The annual best'', ''a3 ECO'' No. 11/2007 of 31 October 2007.</ref>

* [[Wolfgang Clement]] honored Trenkwalder's German subsidiary in the “Top Job 2008” competition as one of the top 100 medium-sized employers.<ref>Clement honors Trenkwalder, [[Wormser Zeitung]] of 23 June 2008.</ref>

* In 2010, Trenkwalder's German subsidiary participated in the “Germany's Best Employers” competition, and it was awarded at the beginning of 2011.<ref>''Trenkwalder honored as an attractive employer'', ''Rheinische Post'' of 8 March 2011; {{cite web|access-date=2016-08-22 |title=Printed Matter 17/12778: Response of the Federal Government to the Small Inquiry of Members of Parliament Klaus Ernst, Jutta Krellmann, Sabine Zimmermann, other members of parliament and the DIE LINKE parliamentary group – Printed Matter 17/12569 – Use of temporary workers at Amazon |url=https://dip21.bundestag.de/dip21/btd/17/127/1712778.pdf |website=German Bundestag, 17th legislative period, printed matter}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

* The "Career’s Best Recruiter" award in gold and silver has been awarded multiple times to the Austrian and German subsidiaries since 2011.<ref>''Career’s Best Recruiters: Heer, Bawag, Trenkwalder, Bosch, RHI'', ''Kurier'' of 4 February 2012; ''Trenkwalder best recruiter in Austria'', ''Oberösterreichische Nachrichten'' of 8 February 2014; ''Did you hear? Gold for Trenkwalder'', ''Kleine Zeitung'' of 7 February 2015; ''Trenkwalder is "Golden Best Recruiter" 2015'', ''Kurier'' of 16 April 2015.</ref>

* In 2012, the company was admitted to the “Leitbetriebe Austria” circle, which represents the top of the Austrian economy.

* In the BEST RECRUITERS Study 2022/2023, Trenkwalder was awarded the BEST RECRUITERS Silver Seal for its above-average recruiting performance.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-10-04 |title=Erfolgreiches Recruiting in herausfordernden Zeiten: Trenkwalder gehört zu Deutschlands krisenfestesten Unternehmen und wurde erneut mit dem BEST RECRUITERS Siegel in Silber ausgezeichnet |url=https://www.pressebox.de/pressemitteilung/trenkwalder-personaldienste-gmbh/Erfolgreiches-Recruiting-in-herausfordernden-Zeiten-Trenkwalder-gehoert-zu-Deutschlands-krisenfestesten-Unternehmen-und-wurde-erneut-mit-dem-BEST-RECRUITERS-Siegel-in-Silber-ausgezeichnet/boxid/1130355 |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=www.pressebox.de |language=de-DE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-14 |title=BEST RECRUITER 2022/2023: Trenkwalder für überdurchschnittliche Recruiting-Leistung erneut mit BEST RECRUITERS Siegel in Silber ausgezeichnet |url=https://www.pressebox.de/pressemitteilung/trenkwalder-personaldienste-gmbh/BEST-RECRUITER-2022-2023-Trenkwalder-fuer-ueberdurchschnittliche-Recruiting-Leistung-erneut-mit-BEST-RECRUITERS-Siegel-in-Silber-ausgezeichnet/boxid/1172257 |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=www.pressebox.de |language=de-DE}}</ref>

* Trenkwalder was awarded the TOP COMPANY seal for the good feedback from employees on German-speaking KUNUNU platform.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-16 |title=Trenkwalder Personaldienste als Arbeitgeber: Gehalt, Karriere, Benefits |url=https://www.kununu.com/de/trenkwaldergmbh |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=kununu.com |language=de}}</ref>

== Board of directors ==
Mark Pollok is a German manager, graduated in industrial engineering from RWTH Aachen and current CEO of Trenkwalder Group AG.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2022-12-28 |title=Mark Pollok Appointed CEO of Trenkwalder Group AG |url=https://www.pressebox.de/pressemitteilung/trenkwalder-personaldienste-gmbh/Mark-Pollok-zum-CEO-der-Trenkwalder-Group-AG-ernannt/boxid/1140726 |access-date=2024-07-23 |language=de-DE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Salzburger Nachrichten |date=2023-09-21 |title=Professionals Sought Worldwide |url=https://www.sn.at/leben/karriere/oesterreich-fachkraefte-ausland-145664086 |access-date=2024-07-23 |language=de}}</ref> He joined Trenkwalder Group AG in 2017 and soon became Managing Director of the German Trenkwalder companies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mark Pollok stieg im Vorstand zum CEO auf |url=https://www.gewinn.com/artikel/mark-pollok-stieg-im-vorstand-zum-ceo-auf |access-date=2024-07-23 |website=GEWINN |language=de-DE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mark Pollok Appointed CEO of Trenkwalder Group AG |url=https://www.leadersnet.at/news/65427,mark-pollok-zum-ceo-der-trenkwalder-group-ag-ernannt.html |access-date=2024-07-23 |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Angelika.Gross |date=2022-12-10 |title=Skills Shortage: When Personnel Consultants Can No Longer Find Personnel |url=https://kurier.at/wirtschaft/karriere/fachkraeftemangel-wenn-personalberater-kein-personal-mehr-finden/402252987 |access-date=2024-07-23 |language=de}}</ref>
